body.en: A linear relationship changes at a constant rate — its graph is a straight line. Mastering lines is the foundation for everything from SAT word problems to the slope fields of calculus.
body.ar: A linear relationship changes at a الثابت rate — its التمثيل البياني is a straight line. Mastering lines is the foundation for everything from SAT word problems to the الميل fields of التفاضل والتكامل.

body.en: A linear equation in one variable has the form \( ax+b=0 \) with \( a\neq 0 \); its single solution is \( x=-\dfrac{b}{a} \). In two variables, \( y=mx+b \) describes a line of slope \( m \) and \( y \)-intercept \( b \).
body.ar: A المعادلة الخطية in one المتغير has the form \( ax+b=0 \) with \( a\neq 0 \); its single الحل is \( x=-\dfrac{b}{a} \). In two المتغيرات, \( y=mx+b \) describes a line of الميل \( m \) and \( y \)-المقطع \( b \).

body.en: Euclidean Invariants, Locus Equations & Scaling Laws: In analytic geometry, geometric loci translate into algebraic constraints via Euclidean distance \(d = \sqrt{(x_2-x_1)^2 + (y_2-y_1)^2}\). A circle of center \((h, k)\) and radius \(r\) satisfies \((x-h)^2 + (y-k)^2 = r^2\), and a tangent line at point \(P\) is strictly perpendicular to the radius \(CP\) (\(m_{\text{tan}} \cdot m_{\text{rad}} = -1\)). Under a similarity scale factor \(k\), all linear lengths scale by \(k\), surface areas scale by \(k^2\), and volumes scale by \(k^3\).
body.ar: Euclidean Invariants, Locus المعادلات & Scaling Laws: In analytic الهندسة, geometric loci translate into algebraic constraints via Euclidean distance \(d = \sqrt{(x_2-x_1)^2 + (y_2-y_1)^2}\). A الدائرة of center \((h, k)\) and نصف القطر \(r\) satisfies \((x-h)^2 + (y-k)^2 = r^2\), and a خط المماس at point \(P\) is strictly perpendicular to the نصف القطر \(CP\) (\(m_{\text{tan}} \cdot m_{\text{rad}} = -1\)). Under a similarity scale factor \(k\), all linear lengths scale by \(k\), surface areas scale by \(k^2\), and volumes scale by \(k^3\).

body.en:
Why Inscribed Angles Equal Half the Central Angle & Circle Completion Works: Given \(x^2 + y^2 + 2gx + 2fy + c = 0\), completing the square in \(x\) and \(y\) simultaneously yields:

\[ (x + g)^2 - g^2 + (y + f)^2 - f^2 + c = 0 \implies (x + g)^2 + (y + f)^2 = g^2 + f^2 - c \]

Thus the center is \((-g, -f)\) and the radius is \(r = \sqrt{g^2 + f^2 - c}\) (requiring \(g^2 + f^2 > c\)). In any circle, drawing diameter \(POQ\) splits an inscribed angle \(\angle APB\) into two isosceles triangles \(\triangle OAP\) and \(\triangle OBP\) (since \(OA = OB = OP = r\)); by the exterior angle theorem, \(\angle AOB = 2\angle APB\).
body.ar:
Why Inscribed Angles Equal Half the Central الزاوية & الدائرة Completion Works: المعطيات \(x^2 + y^2 + 2gx + 2fy + c = 0\), completing the square in \(x\) and \(y\) simultaneously yields:

\[ (x + g)^2 - g^2 + (y + f)^2 - f^2 + c = 0 \implies (x + g)^2 + (y + f)^2 = g^2 + f^2 - c \]

Thus the center is \((-g, -f)\) and the نصف القطر is \(r = \sqrt{g^2 + f^2 - c}\) (requiring \(g^2 + f^2 > c\)). In any الدائرة, drawing القطر \(POQ\) splits an inscribed الزاوية \(\angle APB\) into two isosceles triangles \(\triangle OAP\) and \(\triangle OBP\) (since \(OA = OB = OP = r\)); by the exterior الزاوية المبرهنة, \(\angle AOB = 2\angle APB\).

الشرح الرياضي (المعادلات الخطية ومعادلات المستقيم):

Solve \( 3x+5=20 \).

Subtract 5, then divide by 3:

body.en:
Find the line through \( (1,2) \) and \( (5,10) \).

Slope first, then point–slope with \( (1,2) \):

\[ m=\frac{10-2}{5-1}=2, \qquad y-2=2(x-1)\;\Longrightarrow\; y=2x. \]
body.ar:
Find the line through \( (1,2) \) and \( (5,10) \).

Slope first, then point–الميل with \( (1,2) \):

\[ m=\frac{10-2}{5-1}=2, \qquad y-2=2(x-1)\;\Longrightarrow\; y=2x. \]

label.en: ⚠ Common traps — Undefined slopes & reversing inequality signs
label.ar: ⚠ Common traps — Undefined slopes & reversing المتباينة signs

body.en:
Vertical vs horizontal lines: A horizontal line \( y = b \) has zero slope (\( m = 0 \)). A vertical line \( x = a \) has an undefined slope (division by zero: \( \Delta x = 0 \)) and cannot be written in slope-intercept form \( y = mx + b \).

Perpendicular slopes: Perpendicular lines have negative reciprocal slopes: \( m_2 = -\dfrac{1}{m_1} \) (meaning \( m_1 \cdot m_2 = -1 \)). Simply negating without inverting is a frequent mistake.

Inequality sign reversal: Whenever you multiply or divide both sides of an inequality by a negative number, always reverse the inequality symbol (e.g., -2x < 8 \implies x > -4 ).
body.ar:
Vertical vs horizontal lines: A horizontal line \( y = b \) has zero الميل (\( m = 0 \)). A vertical line \( x = a \) has an undefined الميل (division by zero: \( \Delta x = 0 \)) and cannot be written in الميل-المقطع form \( y = mx + b \).

Perpendicular slopes: Perpendicular lines have negative reciprocal slopes: \( m_2 = -\dfrac{1}{m_1} \) (meaning \( m_1 \cdot m_2 = -1 \)). Simply negating without inverting is a frequent mistake.

Inequality sign reversal: Whenever you multiply or divide both sides of an المتباينة by a negative number, always reverse the المتباينة symbol (e.g., -2x < 8 \implies x > -4 ).

label.en: Worked Example \(C\) — Linear Equations & Lines (Medium Application)
label.ar: مثال محلول \(C\) — المعادلات الخطية & Lines (Medium Application)

body.en:
Problem (Medium): In the \(xy\)-plane, line \(\ell\) passes through the points \((-2, 5)\) and \((4, -1)\). Line \(k\) is perpendicular to line \(\ell\) and has the equation \(ax + 2y = c\), where \(a\) and \(c\) are constants. If line \(k\) passes through the point \((3, 1)\), what is the value of \(c\)?

Step-by-Step Solution: First, find the slope of line \(\ell\) using the slope formula: \[ m_\ell = \frac{-1 - 5}{4 - (-2)} = \frac{-6}{6} = -1 \] Since line \(k\) is perpendicular to line \(\ell\), its slope \(m_k\) is the negative reciprocal of \(m_\ell\): \[ m_k = -\frac{1}{-1} = 1 \] Next, rewrite the standard form equation of line \(k\), \(ax + 2y = c\), in slope-intercept form to find the relationship between \(a\) and the slope: \[ 2y = -ax + c \implies y = -\frac{a}{2}x + \frac{c}{2} \] The slope is \(-\frac{a}{2}\). Setting this equal to \(1\): \[ -\frac{a}{2} = 1 \implies a = -2 \] Substitute \(a = -2\) and the point \((3, 1)\) into \(ax + 2y = c\) to solve for \(c\): \[ (-2)(3) + 2(1) = c \implies -6 + 2 = c \implies c = -4 \] Common traps: - Forgetting the negative sign when isolating \(y\) gives \(\frac{a}{2} = 1 \implies a = 2\), which leads to \(2(3) + 2(1) = 8\) (Choice D). - Swapping the coordinates \(x\) and \(y\) when substituting \((3, 1)\) yields \((-2)(1) + 2(3) = 4\) (Choice C).
body.ar:
Problem (Medium): In the \(xy\)-plane, line \(\ell\) passes through the points \((-2, 5)\) and \((4, -1)\). Line \(k\) is perpendicular to line \(\ell\) and has the المعادلة \(ax + 2y = c\), حيث \(a\) and \(c\) are constants. If line \(k\) passes through the point \((3, 1)\), what is the value of \(c\)?

Step-by-Step الحل: First, أوجد ميل line \(\ell\) using the الميل الصيغة: \[ m_\ell = \frac{-1 - 5}{4 - (-2)} = \frac{-6}{6} = -1 \] Since line \(k\) is perpendicular to line \(\ell\), its الميل \(m_k\) is the negative reciprocal of \(m_\ell\): \[ m_k = -\frac{1}{-1} = 1 \] Next, rewrite the standard form المعادلة of line \(k\), \(ax + 2y = c\), in الميل-المقطع form to أوجد relationship between \(a\) and the الميل: \[ 2y = -ax + c \implies y = -\frac{a}{2}x + \frac{c}{2} \] The الميل is \(-\frac{a}{2}\). Setting this equal to \(1\): \[ -\frac{a}{2} = 1 \implies a = -2 \] عوّض \(a = -2\) and the point \((3, 1)\) into \(ax + 2y = c\) to أوجد قيمة \(c\): \[ (-2)(3) + 2(1) = c \implies -6 + 2 = c \implies c = -4 \] Common traps: - Forgetting the negative sign عندما isolating \(y\) gives \(\frac{a}{2} = 1 \implies a = 2\), which leads to \(2(3) + 2(1) = 8\) (Choice D). - Swapping the الإحداثيات \(x\) and \(y\) عندما substituting \((3, 1)\) yields \((-2)(1) + 2(3) = 4\) (Choice C).

label.en: Worked Example \(D\) — Linear Equations & Lines (Hard Application)
label.ar: مثال محلول \(D\) — المعادلات الخطية & Lines (Hard Application)

body.en:
Problem (Hard): In the \(xy\)-plane, line \(\ell_1\) has the equation \(3x + 4y = 24\). Line \(\ell_2\) is perpendicular to \(\ell_1\) and intersects \(\ell_1\) at a point \(P\) in the first quadrant. If line \(\ell_1\), line \(\ell_2\), and the \(x\)-axis enclose a triangle with an area of \(6\), what is the \(x\)-coordinate of \(P\)?

Step-by-Step Solution: Let \(P = (x_0, y_0)\) be the intersection point of lines \(\ell_1\) and \(\ell_2\). Since \(P\) lies in the first quadrant, \(x_0 > 0\) and \(y_0 > 0\). 1. **Find the \(x\)-intercept of \(\ell_1\):** Setting \(y = 0\) in \(3x + 4y = 24\) yields \(3x = 24 \implies x = 8\). Thus, \(\ell_1\) intersects the \(x\)-axis at \(A(8, 0)\). 2. **Find the \(x\)-intercept of \(\ell_2\):** The slope of \(\ell_1\) is \(-\frac{3}{4}\). Since \(\ell_2 \perp \ell_1\), the slope of \(\ell_2\) is the negative reciprocal, \(m_2 = \frac{4}{3}\). The equation of \(\ell_2\) passing through \(P(x_0, y_0)\) is: \[ y - y_0 = \frac{4}{3}(x - x_0) \] Setting \(y = 0\) gives the \(x\)-intercept \(B(x_B, 0)\): \[ -y_0 = \frac{4}{3}(x_B - x_0) \implies x_B = x_0 - \frac{3}{4}y_0 \] 3. **Determine the base of \(\triangle APB\) along the \(x\)-axis:** The length of the base \(AB\) is: \[ AB = 8 - x_B = 8 - \left(x_0 - \frac{3}{4}y_0\right) \] Since \(P(x_0, y_0)\) lies on \(\ell_1\), \(3x_0 + 4y_0 = 24\), which means \(x_0 = 8 - \frac{4}{3}y_0\). Substituting this into the base expression: \[ AB = 8 - \left(8 - \frac{4}{3}y_0 - \frac{3}{4}y_0\right) = \left(\frac{4}{3} + \frac{3}{4}\right)y_0 = \frac{25}{12}y_0 \] 4. **Relate the area to \(y_0\):** The altitude from \(P\) to the base \(AB\) on the \(x\)-axis is the \(y\)-coordinate \(y_0\). The area of \(\triangle APB\) is: \[ \text{Area} = \frac{1}{2} \times \text{base} \times \text{height} = \frac{1}{2} \times \left(\frac{25}{12}y_0\right) \times y_0 = \frac{25}{24}y_0^2 \] Setting the area equal to \(6\): \[ \frac{25}{24}y_0^2 = 6 \implies y_0^2 = \frac{144}{25} \implies y_0 = \frac{12}{5} \] 5. **Find the \(x\)-coordinate of \(P\):** Substitute \(y_0 = \frac{12}{5}\) back into \(3x_0 + 4y_0 = 24\): \[ 3x_0 + 4\left(\frac{12}{5}\right) = 24 \implies 3x_0 + \frac{48}{5} = \frac{120}{5} \] \[ 3x_0 = \frac{72}{5} \implies x_0 = \frac{24}{5} \] Common misconceptions: - Choosing \(\frac{12}{5}\) confuses the \(x\)-coordinate with the \(y\)-coordinate of \(P\). - Choosing \(3\) gives the \(x\)-intercept of line \(\ell_2\) rather than the \(x\)-coordinate of point \(P\).
body.ar:
Problem (Hard): In the \(xy\)-plane, line \(\ell_1\) has the المعادلة \(3x + 4y = 24\). Line \(\ell_2\) is perpendicular to \(\ell_1\) and intersects \(\ell_1\) at a point \(P\) in the first quadrant. If line \(\ell_1\), line \(\ell_2\), and the \(x\)-axis enclose a المثلث with an المساحة of \(6\), what is the \(x\)-الإحداثي of \(P\)?

Step-by-Step الحل: Let \(P = (x_0, y_0)\) be the التقاطع point of lines \(\ell_1\) and \(\ell_2\). Since \(P\) lies in the first quadrant, \(x_0 > 0\) and \(y_0 > 0\). 1. **أوجد \(x\)-المقطع of \(\ell_1\):** Setting \(y = 0\) in \(3x + 4y = 24\) yields \(3x = 24 \implies x = 8\). وعليه, \(\ell_1\) intersects the \(x\)-axis at \(A(8, 0)\). 2. **أوجد \(x\)-المقطع of \(\ell_2\):** The الميل of \(\ell_1\) is \(-\frac{3}{4}\). Since \(\ell_2 \perp \ell_1\), the الميل of \(\ell_2\) is the negative reciprocal, \(m_2 = \frac{4}{3}\). The المعادلة of \(\ell_2\) passing through \(P(x_0, y_0)\) is: \[ y - y_0 = \frac{4}{3}(x - x_0) \] Setting \(y = 0\) gives the \(x\)-المقطع \(B(x_B, 0)\): \[ -y_0 = \frac{4}{3}(x_B - x_0) \implies x_B = x_0 - \frac{3}{4}y_0 \] 3. **حدّد base of \(\triangle APB\) along the \(x\)-axis:** The length of the base \(AB\) is: \[ AB = 8 - x_B = 8 - \left(x_0 - \frac{3}{4}y_0\right) \] Since \(P(x_0, y_0)\) lies on \(\ell_1\), \(3x_0 + 4y_0 = 24\), which means \(x_0 = 8 - \frac{4}{3}y_0\). Substituting this into the base العبارة الجبرية: \[ AB = 8 - \left(8 - \frac{4}{3}y_0 - \frac{3}{4}y_0\right) = \left(\frac{4}{3} + \frac{3}{4}\right)y_0 = \frac{25}{12}y_0 \] 4. **Relate the المساحة to \(y_0\):** The altitude from \(P\) to the base \(AB\) on the \(x\)-axis is the \(y\)-الإحداثي \(y_0\). The المساحة of \(\triangle APB\) is: \[ \text{Area} = \frac{1}{2} \times \text{base} \times \text{height} = \frac{1}{2} \times \left(\frac{25}{12}y_0\right) \times y_0 = \frac{25}{24}y_0^2 \] Setting the المساحة equal to \(6\): \[ \frac{25}{24}y_0^2 = 6 \implies y_0^2 = \frac{144}{25} \implies y_0 = \frac{12}{5} \] 5. **أوجد \(x\)-الإحداثي of \(P\):** عوّض \(y_0 = \frac{12}{5}\) back into \(3x_0 + 4y_0 = 24\): \[ 3x_0 + 4\left(\frac{12}{5}\right) = 24 \implies 3x_0 + \frac{48}{5} = \frac{120}{5} \] \[ 3x_0 = \frac{72}{5} \implies x_0 = \frac{24}{5} \] Common misconceptions: - Choosing \(\frac{12}{5}\) confuses the \(x\)-الإحداثي with the \(y\)-الإحداثي of \(P\). - Choosing \(3\) gives the \(x\)-المقطع of line \(\ell_2\) rather than the \(x\)-الإحداثي of point \(P\).

question.en: Find the equation of the line that passes through \( (4, -1) \) and is perpendicular to the line \( 2x - 3y = 9 \). Express your answer in slope-intercept form.
question.ar: أوجد معادلة المستقيم that يمر بالنقطة \( (4, -1) \) and is عمودي على the line \( 2x - 3y = 9 \). Express your answer in slope-intercept form.

solution.en:
1. Find the slope of the given line by converting to slope-intercept form:

\[ -3y = -2x + 9 \implies y = \frac{2}{3}x - 3. \]

The slope of the given line is \( m_1 = \dfrac{2}{3} \).

2. The perpendicular slope is the negative reciprocal:

\[ m_\perp = -\frac{3}{2}. \]

3. Use point-slope form with \( (x_1, y_1) = (4, -1) \):

\[ y - (-1) = -\frac{3}{2}(x - 4) \implies y + 1 = -\frac{3}{2}x + 6 \implies y = -\frac{3}{2}x + 5. \]
solution.ar:
1. أوجد ميل the given line by converting to slope-intercept form:

\[ -3y = -2x + 9 \implies y = \frac{2}{3}x - 3. \]

The slope of the given line is \( m_1 = \dfrac{2}{3} \).

2. The perpendicular slope is the negative reciprocal:

\[ m_\perp = -\frac{3}{2}. \]

3. Use point-slope form with \( (x_1, y_1) = (4, -1) \):

\[ y - (-1) = -\frac{3}{2}(x - 4) \implies y + 1 = -\frac{3}{2}x + 6 \implies y = -\frac{3}{2}x + 5. \]

question.en: Solve the linear inequality \(-3(2x - 4) \le 4x - 8\) and express the solution in interval notation.
question.ar: حل the linear inequality \(-3(2x - 4) \le 4x - 8\) and express the solution in interval notation.

solution.en: Expand the left side: \[-6x + 12 \le 4x - 8.\] Collect all \(x\) terms on one side: \[-10x \le -20.\] Divide both sides by \(-10\) and reverse the inequality symbol: \[x \ge 2.\] In interval notation: \([2, \infty)\).

solution.en:
To find the coordinates of the \(x\)-intercept, substitute \(y = 0\) into the equation \(4x - 7y = 28\):

\[
4(c) - 7(0) = 28
\]
\[

\]
\[

- Choice A is correct.
- Choice B (\(-4\)) is the result of solving for the \(y\)-intercept by setting \(x = 0\), yielding \(-7y = 28 \implies y = -4\).

- Choice D (\(28\)) incorrectly takes the constant term as the intercept.

question.en: [Practice 4 · Medium] The graph of the linear equation \(y = mx + c\) is shown below. The line passes through the point \((-3, -11)\) and intersects the y-axis at \((0, k)\). If the slope of the line is \(-3\), determine the value of \(k\).
question.ar: [Practice 4 · Medium] The graph of the linear equation \(y = mx + c\) is shown below. The line يمر بالنقطة the point \((-3, -11)\) and intersects the y-axis at \((0, k)\). إذا كان the slope of the line is \(-3\), حدّد value of \(k\).

hints.en: The equation of a line is given by \(y = mx + c\), where \(m\) is the slope and \(c\) is the y-intercept.
hints.ar: The equation of a line is given by \(y = mx + c\), حيث \(m\) is the slope and \(c\) is the y-intercept.

hints.en: We are given that the slope \(m = -3\). Therefore, the equation of the line is \(y = -3x + c\). The line passes through the point \((-3, -11)\). We can substitute these coordinates into the equation to find \(c\): \(-11 = -3(-3) + c\).
hints.ar: We are إذا علمت أن the slope \(m = -3\). وبالتالي، the equation of the line is \(y = -3x + c\). The line يمر بالنقطة the point \((-3, -11)\). We can عوّض these coordinates into the equation to أوجد \(c\): \(-11 = -3(-3) + c\).

hints.en: Therefore, the line intersects the y-axis at \((0, -20)\).
hints.ar: وبالتالي، the line intersects the y-axis at \((0, -20)\).

solution.en:
The equation of a line is given by \(y = mx + c\), where \(m\) is the slope and \(c\) is the y-intercept. 
We are given that the slope \(m = -3\). Therefore, the equation of the line is \(y = -3x + c\).
The line passes through the point \((-3, -11)\). We can substitute these coordinates into the equation to find \(c\):
\(-11 = -3(-3) + c\)
\(-11 = 9 + c\)
\(c = -11 - 9\)
\(c = -20\)

The y-intercept is the point where the line crosses the y-axis, which is \((0, k)\). For the equation \(y = -3x + c\), when \(x=0\), \(y=c\). Thus, \(k = c\). 
Since \(c = -20\), the value of \(k\) is \(-20\).

Therefore, the line intersects the y-axis at \((0, -20)\).
solution.ar:
The equation of a line is given by \(y = mx + c\), حيث \(m\) is the slope and \(c\) is the y-intercept. 
We are إذا علمت أن the slope \(m = -3\). وبالتالي، the equation of the line is \(y = -3x + c\).
The line يمر بالنقطة the point \((-3, -11)\). We can عوّض these coordinates into the equation to أوجد \(c\):
\(-11 = -3(-3) + c\)
\(-11 = 9 + c\)
\(c = -11 - 9\)
\(c = -20\)

The y-intercept is the point حيث the line crosses the y-axis, which is \((0, k)\). For the equation \(y = -3x + c\), عندما \(x=0\), \(y=c\). وعليه، \(k = c\). 
Since \(c = -20\), the value of \(k\) is \(-20\).

وبالتالي، the line intersects the y-axis at \((0, -20)\).

label.en: ● Master Atlas of the 9 Main Parent Functions & Universal Transformation Law
label.ar: ● الأطلس الشامل للدوال الأم التسع وقانون التحويلات الهندسية العام

body.en:
Every algebraic and elementary transcendental model is built by transforming one of the nine core parent functions via \(g(x) = a\,f(x - h) + k\), where \(|a|\) scales vertically (reflecting across the \(x\)-axis if \(a < 0\)), \(h\) shifts horizontally, and \(k\) shifts vertically:

FamilyTransformed Form \(g(x)\)DomainRange (\(a > 0\))Key Geometric Feature
Constant\(f(x) = c\)\((-\infty, \infty)\)\(\{c\}\)Horizontal line, slope \(0\)
Linear\(a(x - h) + k\)\((-\infty, \infty)\)\((-\infty, \infty)\)Constant slope \(m = a\), pivot \((h, k)\)
Quadratic\(a(x - h)^2 + k\)\((-\infty, \infty)\)\([k, \infty)\)Parabola vertex \((h, k)\), axis \(x = h\)
Cubic\(a(x - h)^3 + k\)\((-\infty, \infty)\)\((-\infty, \infty)\)Inflection center \((h, k)\), S-curve
Absolute Value\(a|x - h| + k\)\((-\infty, \infty)\)\([k, \infty)\)V-corner vertex \((h, k)\), slopes \(\pm a\)
Radical\(a\sqrt{x - h} + k\)\([h, \infty)\)\([k, \infty)\)Endpoint \((h, k)\), half-parabola
Rational\(\dfrac{a}{x - h} + k\)\(x \neq h\)\(y \neq k\)Vertical asymptote \(x = h\), horizontal \(y = k\)
Exponential\(a \cdot 2^{x - h} + k\)\((-\infty, \infty)\)\((k, \infty)\)Horizontal asymptote \(y = k\), anchor \((h, a+k)\)
Logarithmic\(a\ln(x - h) + k\)\((h, \infty)\)\((-\infty, \infty)\)Vertical asymptote \(x = h\), anchor \((h+1, k)\)
body.ar:
تُبنى النماذج الجبرية والمتسامية الأساسية من خلال تطبيق التحويل القياسي \(g(x) = a\,f(x - h) + k\) على إحدى الدوال الأم التسع، حيث يتحكم \(|a|\) في التمدد الرأسي (مع انعكاس حول محور السينات إذا كان \(a < 0\))، ويمثل \(h\) الإزاحة الأفقية، و\(k\) الإزاحة الرأسية:

عائلة الدالةالصورة المحوّلة \(g(x)\)المجالالمدى (\(a > 0\))السمة الهندسية المميزة
الثابتة\(f(x) = c\)\((-\infty, \infty)\)\(\{c\}\)مستقيم أفقي ميله \(0\)
الخطية\(a(x - h) + k\)\((-\infty, \infty)\)\((-\infty, \infty)\)ميل ثابت \(m = a\) ونقطة ارتكاز \((h, k)\)
التربيعية\(a(x - h)^2 + k\)\((-\infty, \infty)\)\([k, \infty)\)قطع مكافئ رأسه \((h, k)\) ومحوره \(x = h\)
التكعيبية\(a(x - h)^3 + k\)\((-\infty, \infty)\)\((-\infty, \infty)\)نقطة انعطاف مركزية \((h, k)\)
القيمة المطلقة\(a|x - h| + k\)\((-\infty, \infty)\)\([k, \infty)\)رأس زاوي على شكل V عند \((h, k)\) بميلين \(\pm a\)
الجذرية\(a\sqrt{x - h} + k\)\([h, \infty)\)\([k, \infty)\)نقطة بداية \((h, k)\) ومجال مقيّد \(x \ge h\)
النسبية (المقلوب)\(\dfrac{a}{x - h} + k\)\(x \neq h\)\(y \neq k\)تقارب رأسي \(x = h\) وتقارب أفقي \(y = k\)
الأسية\(a \cdot 2^{x - h} + k\)\((-\infty, \infty)\)\((k, \infty)\)تقارب أفقي \(y = k\) ونقطة ارتكاز \((h, a+k)\)
اللوغاريتمية\(a\ln(x - h) + k\)\((h, \infty)\)\((-\infty, \infty)\)تقارب رأسي \(x = h\) ونقطة ارتكاز \((h+1, k)\)
